home.hero_subtitle: BAW is a privacy-first AI stylist that lives entirely in your browser. Drop your wardrobe and a selfie in, get a four-axis verdict in milliseconds, and let any agent collaborate with you through document.modelContext.
home.hero_card_caption: oversized blazer · cropped trouser · white leather sneaker
home.demo_blurb: Drop a flatlay of your outfit and a mirror selfie. BAW scores silhouette, palette, texture and occasion fit in under four seconds — and never sends a single byte outside your device.
home.demo_caption: on-device · 0 uploads · model · baw-vl-1.3b · avg latency · 3.4s
home.demo_note_silhouette: Overall X-shape — shoulder-to-hip ratio near the golden 1:1.4. A belt would harden the waist.
home.demo_note_palette: ~95% greyscale with a 5% silver pop. Textbook BAW — the eye has somewhere to land.
home.demo_note_next: Same white shirt + black trouser, try a black merino turtleneck as the inner layer.
home.pillars_title_emph: It knows why you dressed that way.
home.pillar_1_body: From shoulder drop to hem weight, from wool micron count to leather grain. BAW describes every inch of what you're wearing like a senior buyer would.
home.pillar_2_body: A 120k street-style dataset taught BAW not just whether your outfit is black-and-white, but whether it's advanced black-and-white.
home.pillar_3_body: The same white shirt gets a different verdict on a creative Monday and a banking Friday. BAW knows which room you're walking into.
home.privacy_blurb: The default BAW model runs in your browser. We don't have a database to leak, because we never built one. Open DevTools and watch it not phone home.

home.privacy_3_title: Open the DevTools. Count the requests.
home.privacy_3_body: The BAW client is open source. If you find a single outbound request, we'll send you a year of Studio for free.
home.ritual_1_body: One selfie. BAW reads your body shape, skin tone, hair and energy for the day. No account, no body measurements.
home.ritual_2_body: The vision model understands clothes and people at the same time. Silhouette, palette, fabric, proportion, occasion — plus a one-line verdict.
home.ritual_3_body: Every score becomes part of your wardrobe diary: which pieces you over-wear, which combos you've never tried, where the utilisation curve is climbing.

how.title: Three minutes,
how.lead: BAW runs a 1.3B-parameter vision-language model in WebGPU + WASM, right in your browser. The model loads once, then every outfit scoring call is local — no API key, no cloud round-trip, no privacy footprint.
how.p_signal: Two images go in. The model outputs a four-axis vector — silhouette, palette, texture, occasion fit — plus an overall score 0-10. Every comment is generated against a fashion-specific prompt library we curated with stylists and buyers.
how.p_privacy: We treat your wardrobe the way a good tailor treats your measurements. We don't store them, log them, or upload them. Open DevTools while you score an outfit: zero outbound requests. That's the bar.
how.p_webmcp: The same wardrobe, the same scoring engine — but exposed as native browser tools. An agent you trust can call list_wardrobe, analyze_outfit, propose_outfit, and friends through document.modelContext. You stay in the loop on every destructive call.
loop_items: Day 1: Add the pieces you actually wear.
Day 7: BAW spots the over-wearers and the sleeping giants.
Day 30: Utilisation up, decisions faster, "what do I wear" is no longer a 20-minute problem.
not_items: It's not a shopping tool. We don't link to SKUs.
It's not a social feed. Your looks are yours.
It's not a fashion model. It's a stylist — quiet, specific, accountable.

privacy.title: Your wardrobe. Your face.
privacy.lead: The single product principle at BAW: nothing leaves the device unless you send it.
privacy.p_1: The default scoring engine is a 1.3B-parameter vision-language model that runs in WebGPU + WASM, with a quantised checkpoint that fits on a modern phone NPU. The model loads once, then every inference is local. There is no server-side scoring path in the default config.
privacy.p_2: We do not retain thumbnails, embeddings, intermediate tensors, or "service improvement" copies of any image. The wardrobe and history stores live in your browser's local storage and IndexedDB. They evaporate with the tab.
privacy.p_3: The client is open source. Open DevTools → Network while you score an outfit. Count the outbound requests. We will send a year of Studio to anyone who finds a single unexpected one.
privacy.p_4: When you give an agent access to your BAW, that agent can call tools like list_wardrobe, analyze_outfit, and propose_outfit — but only against the wardrobe that lives in your browser. The agent does not get a copy of your data, only callable handles.
privacy.p_5: The optional Studio tier uses a stronger 7B vision model in the cloud for richer analysis. When you opt in, BAW sends a single request per scoring call, with explicit user confirmation each time, and never trains on your images.
items_6: Anonymous usage of the marketing site (no third-party trackers).
Crash reports, only with your explicit opt-in.
Beta email addresses, only to send you an invite.

lookbook.title: A style diary,
lookbook.lead: Every look below was scored by the on-device model. The first eight are the showcase; the rest are added by the community through save_outfit via WebMCP.
lookbook.bottom_blurb: Add your pieces, score an outfit, and start your own diary. The lookbook below will keep growing as you do.

pricing.title: Free to start.
pricing.lead: The local engine is free forever. We charge for the deeper cloud model, team features, and bespoke fine-tunes.
pricing.faq_1_a: Yes. The default scoring engine runs in your browser via WebGPU + WASM. We never see your images. Open DevTools and watch it not phone home.
pricing.faq_2_a: No. The local engine works without signup. Studio (cloud) does require a login so we can sync your unlimited diary.
pricing.faq_3_a: A new browser standard that lets a page expose structured tools to AI agents. BAW uses it so any trusted agent can call list_wardrobe, analyze_outfit, propose_outfit, and friends — with your approval on every write.
pricing.faq_4_q: Can I use BAW on mobile?
pricing.faq_4_a: Yes. The 1.3B model fits on a modern phone NPU. Older devices fall back to a smaller quantised checkpoint.
plan_free_bullets: Local inference · no signup · core scoring
plan_studio_bullets: 7B vision model in the cloud (login required)
plan_atelier_bullets: Private model fine-tune on your SKU
pricing.cta_thanks: Thanks — we'll be in touch within two weeks.

tools.title: Twelve tools.
tools.title_suffix: Both human and agent in the loop.
tools.lead: When you load any BAW page in a WebMCP-aware browser (Chrome 149+ with the flag, or ChatGPT's in-app browser), these twelve tools are registered on document.modelContext. Below is what the agent actually sees: name, description, JSON Schema input, and the annotation that drives the trust boundary in the UI.
tools.snippet:
await document.modelContext.getTools()
→ [ 12 tools · all with descriptions and JSON Schema ]
tools.driver_title: How to drive them from a real agent
tools.driver_chrome_body: Open chrome://flags/#enable-webmcp-testing, enable the flag, and reload. Open any BAW page; the tools are now visible to the in-browser Gemini. The Inspector extension lets you watch calls live.
tools.driver_chatgpt_body: Open any BAW page from inside chatgpt.com. WebMCP is on by default. Ask the model: "Propose an outfit from my BAW wardrobe for a creative Monday" — it will call the right tool.
